title: A More Lively City
notes: City shade trees now have branching trunks and layered canopies for a more natural look.
Coconut palms at the beach, zoo, and around the city now have hanging fronds, coconuts, and clearer silhouettes.
Palms around Mamak Maju are denser and tidier while staying lightweight for phones.
Every tree has consistent directional variation and stays visible even when an extra model fails to load.

title: Dedicated voice and stronger city connections
notes: Voice now uses a dedicated WebRTC connection, keeping microphone traffic away from gameplay updates.
Silent microphone audio is suppressed to reduce unnecessary traffic.
Player movement updates use less data while keeping appearances and table rosters in sync.
Stalled connections recover automatically, and stale updates no longer build up without a limit.
Voice can reconnect independently, with existing proximity, Party and game privacy rules preserved.
Added connection-quality measurements to help diagnose high ping and voice problems.

title: Settings stay above chat
notes: Settings and other modal windows now appear above city chat, including fullscreen chat on mobile.
Closing a modal preserves your chat messages and expanded state.

title: Smoother voice and clearer table rematches
notes: Old microphone frames are discarded after a freeze, and voice queues are kept short to reduce delayed speech.
Graphics switch to Smooth when low frame rates persist. You can change quality in Settings.
UNO Catch stays usable while your own UNO is armed and tolerates unrelated roster updates without duplicate penalties.
After an UNO match, Back to Ready lobby lets everyone ready up again with a fresh game roster.
Lukis Lah supports up to 9 players at larger tables; smaller tables keep their actual seat capacity.

title: A Calmer City Entrance
notes: Entry loading now stays clear with a large progress bar until the city connection is truly ready.
Watson's, busking, stall, and other location sounds no longer play before the player successfully enters.
The first connection no longer shows a confusing connection-lost or reconnect popup.

title: Simpler Mobile Chat Controls
notes: The fullscreen button only appears while the chat panel is open.
Collapsed chat shows only one clear restore button.

title: Mobile Chat Recovers Cleanly
notes: Closing chat after typing restores the city view all the way to the bottom of the screen.
The game canvas is realigned after the iPhone keyboard closes.
Typing status and the mobile control layout no longer linger after chat collapses.

title: Cleaner Mobile Landing
notes: The landing title now scales cleanly with phone width without clipping.
Text, the entry button, and the postcard are rearranged to avoid overlap on short screens.
Background contrast is increased so content remains readable at every phone size.

title: Lighter, Clearer Entrance
notes: The loading screen now shows the actual phase and percentage until the city is ready.
The first connection shows an entering status; reconnect only appears after a previously successful connection drops.
Location music such as busking, mosque, stall, and vehicle audio now loads only when the player is close enough.

title: Aligned Mamak Chair Metadata
notes: The 3D table asset now stores directions for all 25 chairs matching the game's seating data.
Model export fails when old chair metadata remains, keeping character and model directions aligned.
The model cache key is bumped so players load the complete current asset.

title: Large Table Chair Directions
notes: The Mamak V7 model is rebuilt so all nine 3D chairs match character directions and face the table.
The model cache key is bumped so phone browsers load the fixed model instead of an old copy.
Raycast checks confirm the seat, back, and front space for all nine chairs.

title: Nine Large Table Chairs Face Center
notes: All Large Table chair directions now face the table surface for Werewolf and group games.
Chair backs are aligned with character directions so chair visuals and player positions no longer conflict.

title: Fix Login Crash on Retina Screens
notes: The hidden character preview no longer repeatedly enlarges its canvas on high-resolution phones.
Login and logout no longer grow graphics memory from the hidden preview. Inventory preview still uses the real character.

title: Mobile Login Recovers from Stale Sessions
notes: Stored sessions are now verified with Supabase before the player enters the city.
Expired or broken tokens are cleared and the login form opens without a visible enter-exit auto-refresh loop.
If realtime rejects the session, the player goes straight to login with clear instructions.

title: Mobile Login No Longer Auto-Enters After Logout
notes: A fast tap on Jom, let's go after logout now waits for Supabase to clear the session.
The login modal opens correctly and a stale session no longer enters then ejects the player.

title: Geng and Friends Loading Feel Like a Game
notes: Loading text in the Geng and Friend List panels is replaced by a softly animated avatar, name, status, and action skeleton.
The skeleton adapts to phone and desktop layouts, then disappears as soon as real data or an error message is available.
Loading animation respects reduced motion, and every action stays clearly locked while requests process.

title: GM Instructions Stay Until Turned Off
notes: The /gm message stays in the HUD until the Game Master replaces it or uses /gmoff.
The GM banner no longer disappears when the city is empty and reappears for later joiners.
Only /gmoff removes the banner; /gm clear is shown as a normal message.

title: Profiles Connect Directly to Friends and Chat
notes: Each player profile now has Add Friend and Message actions that reflect friend-request status and online presence.
Profiles opened from Lepak Wall now use the same full view as View Profile on a character.
Add Friend can be sent to an offline Wall author; Message shows offline status and becomes active when they are in the city.

title: Player Invites Return as Party
notes: The player-menu option is now called Invite to Party.

title: Cleaner Player Name Tags
notes: Mic and speaker icons, Geng names, and player names now use separate rows so text no longer overlaps.
The whole name tag is raised slightly so it matches your own tag and does not cover the character's head.

title: Geng Applicant Profiles Can Be Opened
notes: Geng leaders can tap a username in Join Requests to view the profile before deciding.
Approve and Decline remain separate so opening a profile cannot accidentally accept or decline the request.

title: Login Works Again After Logout
notes: Logout now clears the old registration step and opens the correct login form on re-entry.
A player who just finished choosing a character no longer sees a website error when logging back in.

title: Open Geng Shows Leader and Roster
notes: Open Gengs now show the team leader's name and member count.
Tap a Geng for the full roster; every member name opens their profile, including offline members.
The leader receives a realtime notification for each new application, with a number badge showing pending requests.

title: Geng Icon Is Easier to Tell Apart
notes: The Geng icon now uses a crest symbol for a group or guild.
The Friends icon remains an add-friend symbol so the two functions no longer look alike.

title: Friend List Is Clearer and Safer
notes: Add Friend requests, acceptances, and list changes now have a short sound.
New requests show a number badge on the Friends button outside the panel, including after reconnect.
Remove friend now asks for confirmation first to prevent accidental deletion.

title: Full Mobile Chat Is Easier to Use
notes: Full chat on phones now fills the viewport correctly without pushing the composer off-screen.
The message list has its own scroll space, so old messages can be swiped without moving the whole view.
The composer stays at the bottom and rises above the mobile keyboard.

title: Map Feels Like a Whiteboard
notes: The map pans with one finger or mouse so you can explore an area without returning to the default center.
Pinch and wheel zoom stay under the finger or cursor instead of always zooming from the map center.
The reset button restores the original zoom and position; LEGOLAND uses the same behavior.

title: Collision Follows Real Shapes
notes: The open grounds of Masjid Kampung Maju are now walkable; only the prayer hall and tower base block movement.
All cars now use rotated real body footprints, with no huge invisible side wall.
Object contact remains solid at walls and cars without harming teleport, chairs, or city paths.

title: Clearer LEGOLAND, Smoother Game
notes: The minimap and full map switch to the LEGOLAND map inside the park, with attractions, areas, and nearby Gengs.
The game panel can be minimized on desktop and phone so chat and voice stay easy to reach during play.
Normal game tables are standardized to four players; the nine-seat Werewolf table remains.
Ah Tong now moves through the open path in front of Warung Muthu without getting stuck at the shop door.

title: Clearer Note Example
notes: The Note placeholder now uses “e.g. away for a moment” as a clearer example.

title: Simpler Player Notes
notes: The AFK note label in Settings is now simply Note.
Save and clear status messages use the same Note name.

title: Google Can Be Unlinked Safely
notes: Accounts using Google can view and manage their Google connection in Security.
Before unlinking Google, players must set a password through a reset link so the account remains accessible.
The system blocks unlinking when Google is the only login method and clearly shows the process status.

title: Forgot Password Is Available in Security
notes: Players can request a password reset from Security.
The reset link is sent to the account email and returns the player to LepakMamak to choose a new password.
Delivery status is clear and the button is locked while the request processes.

title: Edit Profile Has a Clearer Loading State
notes: Edit Profile shows an animated skeleton while account information loads.
Buttons and fields are clearly locked while loading or saving, with Loading and Saving statuses.
The design stays tidy on desktop and mobile and respects reduced motion.

title: Add Lepak Coin Directly from Geng
notes: If the balance is below 1,000 Lepak Coin to create a Geng, the panel shows the balance and required amount clearly.
The Add Lepak Coin button opens the Shop directly for top-ups or the daily claim.
The flow is responsive on desktop and mobile, and the create button stays locked until the balance is sufficient.

title: Wet Deck Rooftop Lounge Opens
notes: Wet Deck at Hotel Mahkota is reachable by lift for sky dining with KLCC, pool, bar, and indoor lounge views.
Four visitors move in the pool with swim animations and stairs so players can enter and exit without falling to the road.
Eight rooftop tables were added, including a nine-seat Werewolf table using the city's lobby and occupancy.
The Wet Deck lounge has a slow original instrumental that is lowered while a table game is open.

title: Geng Optional and Table Invitations Are Safer
notes: Geng is social-only: group chat, member voice, and friend markers on the minimap work without requiring a Geng for table games.
Table invitations show the game, table, and available space; recipients can go there and choose Join and READY themselves.
Reconnect has a 30-second grace period, the Geng panel shows leader, members, and reconnect status, and only the leader can invite.
Full, expired, started, or changed-session invitations are rejected clearly without auto-seating or auto-enrolment.

title: Add Friend and Friend List
notes: Registered players can now Add Friend from the player menu, with requests safely stored in Supabase.
Friend List separates online and offline friends and offers Accept, Decline, Cancel, and Remove.
The Message button in Friend List opens the existing private chat on desktop and mobile.

title: Reconnect When Connection Drops
notes: The red online marker explains the connection error and offers a Restart button at the lower right.
The Restart card uses the same placement as the update card, stays above the action HUD, and is responsive on mobile.
Automatic reconnect runs in the background while the city tries to recover and the player can restart at any time.

title: Geng, Avatar, and Multiplayer Updated
notes: Create a Geng with 1,000 Lepak Coin, accept member requests, and let only the leader approve or disband.
The onboarding character preview now uses the same 3D avatar as Inventory, with improved headscarf options that cover the neck and shoulders.
Remote players remain visible after teleport, and fullscreen chat stays in front with clear minimize and close controls.
Wall photos can still be posted when OpenAI is unavailable; photos with an explicit result are still rejected.

title: English table games and headscarf wardrobe
notes: Lukis Lah, Poker Kampung, UNO Lepak, and Werewolf now use clear English across their lobbies, actions, rules, and results.
Character wardrobe now includes long headscarves, turbans, short headscarves, shawls, square scarves, satin, and instant styles.
dUCk Luxe and Ruffle are shown as Coming Soon while the live 3D character preview supports rotating the selected look.

title: Character Rotation and a Cleaner Shop
notes: The Inventory character can now rotate 360° with a mouse drag or mobile swipe.
The Shop aligns Equip and Unequip buttons at the bottom of every item card.
The Shop Refresh button is removed so it feels like a game menu rather than a web page.

title: Car Finder and Safer Admin Access
notes: The city map can now find Yusuf Suhair's Porsche Taycan and Daddy Fizal's Porsche 911 GT3 RS using live fleet locations.
Car Finder works in both 2D and 3D map views while keeping zoom controls.
The admin portal now uses Supabase Auth and only allows allowlisted admin accounts.
The LEGOLAND attraction panel remains tappable on mobile even while City Chat is open.

title: More Accurate Game Atmosphere, DMs, and Busking
notes: Werewolf now has night, sleep, roar, growl, dead-player voice, next-turn, and countdown cues using free audio stored in the game.
DMs close and disappear when either player goes offline; the server also rejects messages to players who are gone.
The main busker is now at the PETRONAS frontage, with crowd, collision, and audio distance sharing the same coordinates.
The city map keeps zoom in and zoom out with a wider initial view for large areas such as LEGOLAND.

title: Cleaner Game and Lobby Lifecycle
notes: The countdown is cancelled if a player stands up at the last moment and the participant count drops below the minimum.
Play Again no longer disrupts an active UNO, Poker, or Werewolf game; Lukis Lah keeps the roster that already consented.
The table display is one list: Lobby first, then each game with its artwork and joined-player avatars in the same row.

title: Separate Lobby and Developer Test Tools
notes: Table Lobby is always at the top and only lists seated players who have not joined a game.
Each game has its own player list separating those waiting from those already playing.
The development build has a Developer Option to spawn nearby test users, choose mic and speaker status, and remove your test users.

title: Fairer Lukis Lah, Reconnect-Safe
notes: The Lukis Lah timer pauses for up to 30 seconds when a player disconnects and reconnects, preserving their choice and drawing time.
Only lobby players who press READY enter the game; seated-only players receive no card or turn.
The Lukis Lah READY flow now gives the drawer three word choices as promised.
Old Party voice and invitations can no longer leak answers or join a Party without leader authority.

title: Game Roster Uses Real Character Faces
notes: Players who are seated, waiting in the lobby, or already in a game now appear in separate groups without a confusing 'In' list.
Every indicator uses the player's real face, skin tone, hair, and clothing, including the full-city Werewolf roster.
The voice indicator stays bright and sharp above the game even when the city background is blurred on desktop.

title: Lukis Is Locked to the Game Session
notes: New players wait for the next game. An empty seat gives no access to the current game; original players can still reconnect.

title: Large Table Is Easier to Tap
notes: The game button prioritizes the table you are sitting at, with a larger touch area and a stable position while pressed.

title: Play Again Keeps the Table Party Together
notes: Play Again for Lukis Lah! starts a new round without removing the players from the game.
The roster and table positions stay together even if only one player presses Play Again.
Werewolf creates a new game ID and deals fresh roles after the village ends; the village reset stays with the host.

title: Cleaner Chat, Voice, and Busking
notes: City chat stays above action prompts such as Stand with bright, clear text while a table game is open.
The speaking-player indicator moves to the lower right above the KM/H meter with a responsive layout.
The voice marker lights with voice strength and darkens when a nearby player is no longer speaking.
Busking Santai moves to the PETRONAS frontage so the performance is on the station forecourt.

title: Live, Real Character Wardrobe
notes: The wardrobe preview uses the same 3D character model as the live city character.
Choosing a shirt or trousers changes the world character and wardrobe preview immediately without a separate 2D simulation.

title: City Map Opens in 3D
notes: The expanded city map now opens in 3D for easier reading and exploration.
A 2D toggle remains available for the top-down map when needed.

title: Cleaner Speedometer and KLCC Lift
notes: The panel behind the speed and KM/H numbers is removed so the speedometer is transparent again.
The display stays light on desktop, phone, and tablet without a box or extra shadow.
The KLCC lift can descend after reaching the rooftop, even after the player moves slightly on the upper platform.
The lift panel shows seconds while travelling and STOP when stopped at the rooftop.

title: Clearer Taycan Name and VRG9405 Plate
notes: The Porsche Taycan shows Yusuf Suhair's name above the car.
The VRG9405 plate uses a black background and white text like the GT3 RS plate.
The Daddy Fizal label on the GT3 RS is lowered so it does not collide with the player's name inside the car.

title: VRG9405 Plate for Taycan
notes: The Porsche Taycan Frozen Berry now uses the VRG9405 plate on the front and rear.

title: GT3 RS Spoiler Matches the Roofline
notes: The Daddy Fizal GT3 RS spoiler is lowered so it does not rise above the car roofline.
The supports, endplate, and PORSCHE lettering move down together so the aero shape stays clean.

title: Daddy Fizal's GT3 RS in Rembayung
notes: A red Porsche 911 GT3 RS with Daddy Fizal's name and SL45 plate is now available at the Rembayung forecourt.
The car can be claimed, driven, and released in realtime through the authoritative fleet.

title: Porsche Taycan Frozen Berry in Rembayung
notes: The Porsche Taycan Frozen Berry is now displayed at the Rembayung forecourt and can be driven by players.
The car uses the same authoritative vehicle claim, so players can safely claim and release it in realtime.

title: Sports Courts Behind Pantai Senja
notes: The Pickleball and Basket Lepak courts are now behind Pantai Senja, so the beach is no longer directly beside the mosque.
Masjid Kampung Maju moves to the old court area; the map pin, teleport, chairs, and recitation audio follow the new location.

title: Teleport Directly to Pantai Senja
notes: Pantai Senja is now an official teleport destination with an arrival point on the beach entrance path.
The map pin and teleport server now use the same beach coordinates.

title: Loungers and Hammocks at Pantai Senja
notes: Beach chairs and hammocks can now be used for lying down. Each spot is shared live so players do not overlap.
The Mat Kool stall is now at Pantai Senja, with ice-cream audio heard only when you are nearby.

title: Beach Outside the Courts, Waves, and Palms
notes: Pantai Senja tables move from the basketball and pickleball courts to the eastern shoreline.
Moving waves, a coconut booth with an attendant, walking NPCs, and two nine-seat tables complete the beach hangout.

title: Relax at Pantai Senja
notes: Pantai Senja opens southeast of the city with sand, sea, umbrellas, lights, and a campfire.
Four beach tables use the same mamak games, including a nine-seat Werewolf table. Find Pantai Senja on the map.

title: Full Call at the Counter
notes: The original volume of the two-ringgit call is restored at the counter, while the sound stays fully silent beyond five metres.

title: Stall Voice Is Closer and Quieter
notes: The two-ringgit call is now audible only when you are close to the stall counter, with a lower maximum volume.

title: Vendor Voice Returns to the Stalls
notes: The two-ringgit call is now heard near Air Balang Pak Din and Pisang Goreng Mak Cik, loud at the counter and fading as you move away.

title: Public health page
notes: A public LepakMamak health page shows realtime availability, server uptime, latency, current version and live player totals without exposing memory, bandwidth or room names.

title: A Livelier City, Clearer Voice
notes: Fullscreen chat stays expanded until you restore its window size.
The chat minimise and fullscreen controls now sit together on the right side of the header.
Every Lamborghini now drives through the city. Its quieter exhaust follows the moving car and fades with distance.
Your microphone range is brighter and visible over raised floors. The distance ring hides for party speech, which reaches your party across the city.
Seated players get a warning after four and a half minutes without input. At five minutes they leave the table game and release their seat while staying in the city. Move or tap to stay.
Logging out immediately leaves UNO and Werewolf; interrupted connections keep their reconnect grace period.
KFC and McDonald's replace repeated convenience shops, each with an open drive-through lane, order board and collection window.
A Shell station with Shell Select, pumps and a driveable forecourt opens near the eastern LRT line.
Malaysia's second mosque model is now Gereja Harapan. Masjid Kampung Maju remains, and the call to prayer now comes only from that mosque.

title: Lamborghini in Front of the Mamak
notes: A Lamborghini is parked at the kerb outside Mamak Maju. Walk near it and you can hear the exhaust idling; it fades out as you walk away.
You cannot claim a Lamborghini. Walk up to one — parked or out in traffic — and the action button says Not allowed and stays greyed out.

title: Visible Votes, Seer Notes, and UNO That Knows When to End
notes: Werewolf: you can now watch the vote as it happens — how many have pointed at each suspect, and how many want the accused gone. It counts heads, so the Mayor's double vote stays secret until the very end.
Werewolf: the Seer keeps every night's reading instead of only the newest one, so what you learned on the first night is still in front of you on the fourth.
Werewolf: the host can now pick any village from five to nine players. Five, six and eight were always playable, but the panel only ever offered seven or nine.
UNO: a match between two players now finishes at 200 points, and three players at 300, instead of asking everyone for 500. Two people needed about eighteen rounds to get there.
UNO: when a round ends, every losing hand turns face up with what it cost, so you can see where the winner's points came from. You can also sort your hand by colour.
UNO: after someone wins a whole match, everyone can run it back from the table again. The button was there but nothing happened when you pressed it.

title: Chat Button Returns to the Corner
notes: The chat window controls sit together in the top-left corner now, ahead of the title, instead of the expand button floating over the middle of the bar.
The minimise button is back, next to maximise. Clicking the chat header still works the same way.

title: Werewolf Supports Eight and Nine Players
notes: A Werewolf game with 8 or 9 players never actually started — the countdown finished and nothing happened. Every size from 5 to 9 works now, which also means Alpha, Knight, Princess, Hunter and Mayor are reachable for the first time.

title: One Chat, from City to Table
notes: You can read and send chat while playing a table game. The chat box follows you into the game and back out again, keeping your tabs, your unread counts and where you had scrolled to.
New TABLE channel: sit at a table and your messages go to the people at that table. Stand up and you are back to city chat.
Party and private messages are now closed while a Werewolf or Lukis round is running, and a dead Werewolf player's microphone is muted until the game ends. Both were being used to give the game away.

title: Small Fix at ZUS
notes: Teleporting to ZUS Coffee could drop you standing on one of the pavement tables. The tables now sit tucked against the shopfront, clear of where you arrive.

title: See Who Is Where
notes: Walk up to a table and it tells you who is sitting there by name, not just how many.
The Large Table was telling everyone it had three seats. It has nine. Every table now counts its own chairs.
The top left shows who else is in the city at a glance, without opening anything.
In a game lobby, a player who is not ready yet says so. Before, ready showed a tick and not-ready showed nothing at all.

title: Lukis Lah Moves, Every Game Shares One Sound
notes: Lukis Lah reacts at the moments between drawing: a correct guess, the word being revealed, the round results, and a score that just moved. Only the score that changed reacts, not the whole board.
All four table games now share one sound engine, so every game can have its own voice without inventing one.

title: Werewolf Has Night and Day
notes: Werewolf looks like the time of day now. Night is dark and blue, the discussion warms up, judgment turns red, and night falling or day breaking sweeps across the whole panel with a sound to match.
The ending is a proper reveal instead of one line of text: who won, and what everybody actually was. It shows roles, never who voted for whom.

title: Poker Kampung Has Feeling
notes: Poker moves and makes noise now. The flop, turn and river flip onto the felt instead of appearing, the pot jumps when it grows, the seat whose turn it is glows, and the showdown lands with a flourish. Cards land, chips click, and winning has a sound.
Only the cards that just turned over move — the ones already on the table stay put.

title: Touch Feedback on Screen
notes: Tapping anywhere that is not a button now leaves a small ring where your finger landed, so the screen answers you even when there was nothing there to press.

title: Walk Inside the Train
notes: You can walk around inside the LRT carriage now instead of being stuck in your seat for the whole ride. Other passengers see you move about, and you cannot walk out through the walls.

title: Three-Step Sign-Up
notes: Signing up is three steps now: make the account, pick your name, then make your character. Before, the sign-up form asked for your name and your whole character before the account existed.
Signing up with Google goes through the same two steps, so everyone picks their own name and face whichever way they joined.

title: Geng Name Above Your Head
notes: Set a geng name in Settings and it appears in small letters just above your name, for everyone to see. It stays on your device between sessions, guests included.
The expanded chat window now sits in the middle of the screen instead of hanging off the bottom, and the padding inside the panel lines up.

title: Tablet Layout Fixed
notes: On tablets the chat box and the speedometer were sitting on top of the thumbstick and the action buttons. Every layout rule written for tablets was switched off on the tablets it was written for — an iPad with a keyboard attached was being treated as a desktop. Chat now sits clear above the stick, and the speed above the buttons.
Chat can be blown up to fill the screen on a phone too, not just on a computer. The same button closes it.

title: Cleaner Settings
notes: Settings is called Settings now, with a × in the corner to close it. The two lines of filler above it are gone; the version stays.
The settings button is a gear instead of two bars.
The keyboard hints along the bottom now really do stay off on phones and tablets. They were being hidden by an instruction the stylesheet quietly overruled, so they kept showing up on iPads.

title: One Top-Right Menu on Phones
notes: On a phone, the buttons in the top right corner now live behind one ⋮ button. Tap it and they drop down underneath; tap anything, or anywhere else, and it folds away again. On a bigger screen the row stays as it was.

title: Chat Shows Where Everyone Is
notes: Every chat message now shows where the person was standing when they said it, in small letters under their name.
The minimize button has gone from the chat bar. Clicking the header does the same thing, so there was no need for both.

title: No More Stale Versions
notes: If you leave the game open while a new version goes out, it now tells you and refreshes itself: FULL REFRESH BY SYSTEM IN 3, 2, 1. No more playing an old build without knowing.
If the refresh does not pick the new version up, it stops trying and offers you a button instead of reloading over and over.

title: Sign In with Google
notes: You can now sign in with Google instead of making a password.

Your Google name is not used. After signing in you pick the name the city knows you by, and your character's look, exactly like anyone registering with an email. Nothing from your Google profile is copied across.

title: Quiet Police
notes: The police siren is gone for good. Patrol cars still drive around with their lights on, and you can still claim one — they just do it quietly now.

title: City No Longer Over Capacity
notes: When a lot of people arrived at the same moment, a room could go past its limit — up to 120 people in a city built for 100, which is what makes everyone lag. Arrivals are now counted at the moment someone actually walks in.
Logging in twice at the same instant could also leave two of you standing in the city. The older session now steps aside properly.

title: ZUS Coffee Opens in Kampung Maju
notes: ZUS Coffee has opened where the nearer 99 Speedmart used to be — cobalt front, white lettering and a glazed shopfront with the counter visible inside.
Three tables with twelve seats sit on the pavement outside, in the shop's own blue and white. You can sit at any of them, and the map now points at ZUS instead of the old shop.

title: This Week's Board on Lepak Wall
notes: The Lepak Wall now has a weekly board: the top five for basketball points and for time spent at mamak tables. It resets every Monday morning, so a quiet week is never a lost cause.

Punches, recalls, dances and logins are counted for your own profile but are not ranked. A public ranking of punches would just reward punching people, and the rest can be racked up alone in a corner.

title: Street-Light Switches Are Easier to Reach
notes: Walking up to a street lamp gives you the switch far more reliably. You can reach it from a little further back, and a car driving past no longer takes the button away from the lamp you are standing at. All sixty lamps in the city work the same way.

title: Internal Maintenance Update
notes: Housekeeping: the city server is now always published from the released code, so a change someone is still working on can no longer reach the live city by accident.

title: City Server Reports Its Own Health
notes: Behind the scenes, the city server now reports what it is actually doing — how many people are connected, how much it is sending each second, and whether it is starting to struggle — so a busy night gets noticed before anybody's game stutters.

title: One Character Screen, Shop in the Top Bar
notes: Inventory and wardrobe are one screen now. Your character stands in the middle, what you have equipped is on the left, and the grid on the right holds your items and your clothes together — Tops and Bottoms are just two more tabs. There is no separate wardrobe to open any more.
Picking a top or bottoms puts it on straight away and saves it. No Save button, no Cancel.
Shop has its own button in the top bar. The row now reads Wall, centre camera, Shop, Character, Settings.

title: Every Street Light Has Its Own Switch
notes: Street lamps are switched at the lamp now, not from a button in the corner. Walk up to any lamp and the prompt offers Turn on or Turn off.
Each lamp keeps its own state, and everybody in the city sees it change straight away. Night still lights the street by itself; a lamp somebody switched keeps whatever they left it on.

title: Security: Change Password, Delete Account
notes: Settings has a Security panel now. You can change your password there — it asks for your current one first, so a browser somebody left open cannot lock you out of your own account.

You can also delete your account. It removes your account, your items, your posts, your guestbook entries and your messages, and it cannot be undone, so you have to type DELETE to confirm. Guests do not see the panel; there is no account to change.

title: Rain Can Be Reopened, Settings Are Easier to Reach
notes: The Rain over KL switch is back. The Game Master weather panel had been taking its place in settings, which quietly removed the switch for everyone. Once you touch it, it stays where you put it instead of following the live weather, and the sky matches what is falling.
What's new now shows the newest three releases with a button for older ones. The full list had grown long enough to push Return to Mamak Maju off the bottom of a phone screen.

title: Game-Style Scrollbars
notes: Every panel that scrolls — chat, inventory, settings, the wall, the map — now uses one brass rail that matches the game instead of the browser's plain grey bar. The cream panels get a lighter version of it, and phones and tablets get a slimmer one.

title: Tap Outside to Close Settings
notes: Settings now closes when you tap the darkened city around the panel, not only on Resume or Esc. Dragging a scrollbar or selecting text inside the panel will not dismiss it.

title: GM Chakra Stays Visible on Mamak Floors
notes: The glowing seal under the Game Master used to disappear the moment he stepped off the road onto the mamak floor, because that floor stands a little higher than the street. It now draws on top of whatever he is standing on.

title: Private Messages Have Their Own Space
notes: Private messages have moved out of the channel list into their own row above the chat log. Each conversation is a chip with the person's name and its own unread count, and you close it from there.

The channel list is now only about who sees your message: ALL and PARTY. While you are in a private conversation the box states who you are writing to and stops being a menu, so a private line cannot go to the whole city by mistake.

title: City Light Switches, One Character Screen
notes: Street lights now have a switch anyone can flip, in the top bar next to your inventory. Night still turns them on by itself, but whoever flips it, the whole city sees it straight away.

Inventory and wardrobe are one character screen now. Your items, what you have equipped, and the clothes you are wearing sit together, with Wardrobe and Shop buttons right there. The old Refresh button is gone.
Scrolling back through chat no longer snaps you to the newest line. A small arrow appears instead, and one tap brings you back to the latest.

title: The Game Master Has Wings
notes: The Game Master now floats just above the ground with a slow rise and fall, one dark wing and one pale one fanned behind, over a slowly turning seal. Everyone in the city sees it, not just the Game Master.
The city now holds a hundred people at once, up from forty.

title: PETRONAS Pin Is Back in the Right Place
notes: The PETRONAS marker on the city map now sits on the forecourt itself instead of nine metres north of it on empty ground.

title: Werewolf Works with Five Players
notes: Werewolf now plays with as few as five people instead of seven, with one wolf against four and both the seer and the doctor still in.
Any group from five to nine works, so nobody is turned away for being an awkward number.
An empty seat at a table now invites your Party straight into party chat.
The big table at Mamak Maju sits on proper paving instead of the grass beside it.

title: Table and Announcement Fixes
notes: Fixed Werewolf and UNO not starting from the table: everyone who tapped READY is now actually dealt into the game.
A Game Master announcement now really does greet people who join afterwards, instead of only those already online.
The table lobby stopped chattering to every seated player twenty times a second, which was quietly eating mobile data and battery.

title: Large Table for Werewolf
notes: A big nine-seat table has opened at Mamak Maju, so a whole Werewolf village can sit together instead of scattering across the small tables.

title: GM Announcements Stay at the Top
notes: A Game Master announcement now stays at the top of the screen until it is replaced or taken down, and anyone who joins afterwards still sees it.

title: Better iPad Play
notes: The game now lays itself out properly on a tablet: bigger buttons you can actually hit with a thumb, and the joystick, chat and speedometer no longer sit on top of each other.
If you are playing on a touch screen, the game stops telling you to press keys you do not have.

title: Police Enter the City
notes: Two police cars now patrol the city, siren and all. You only hear them when they are near — and yes, you can still claim them.
A connection meter next to the player count shows your signal and your ping in milliseconds.
When someone talks, their name and face appear under the map, so you always know who is speaking.

title: Cleaner Chat, GM Can Tell Everyone
notes: Chat channels moved into the typing bar: tap the button on the left to switch between everyone, your party, or a private message.
On a computer you can now blow the chat up into a proper window instead of squinting at the corner.
The Game Master can announce something to the whole city, and it scrolls across the top before landing in chat so nobody misses it.

title: New Tables, Walkable Bridge
notes: Every table game now works the same way: sit, pick a game, tap READY, and a three-two-one count-in deals you in. Rematch without leaving your seat.
Werewolf now says plainly that it gathers the whole city instead of pretending to be your table.
You can walk across the Saloma Link. Take the steps up at either end — the road underneath still runs as normal.
The city now holds forty people instead of twenty-four.

title: Geng, Voice, and Street Lights
notes: Right-click anyone to invite them into your party or send them a private message.
Your microphone and speakers can be set to your Party only, so you can talk to your Party while still hearing the mamak.
Everyone online shows on the map as a dot — light blue for the city, red for your party.
Street lights come on at night, and the streets are no longer pitch black.
Chat opens with Enter and tucks away after you send, so the screen stays clear.

title: LepakMamak City
notes: Explore a small Kuala Lumpur: the mamak restaurant, shops, mosque, and surrounding neighbourhood.
Ride the LRT across eight stations, or take a motorbike or car and race your friends.
Table games at the mamak: Lukis Lah!, Poker Kampung, UNO Lepak and Werewolf.
City chat, voice chat with whoever is nearby, and the Lepak Wall for photos and voice notes.
